intended_object: The left section functor C → C × D, X ↦ (X, Z), f ↦ (f, id_Z), for a fixed object Z of D. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition sends each object X to (X, Z) and each morphism f to f ×ₘ 𝟙 Z, which is the pair (f, 𝟙 Z) in the product category. Functoriality holds because identities and composition in C × D are computed componentwise. This is exactly the standard functor "include C at the slice Z".

It works for arbitrary categories at arbitrary universe levels, so it is at its natural generality. It is the same functor as `(𝟭 C).prod' ((Functor.const C).obj Z)`, but Mathlib has no separate named definition of it other than this one.
